journeys.title: Bachelor's then master's in the US, with post-completion OPT after each and a transfer between schools in the grace period
journeys.timeline:
2019-08-26 BS Economics (not STEM) begins at School A, SEVP-certified university. I-20 level: bachelor's.
2023-02-11 to 2023-07-11 BS OPT filing window (computed: program end minus 90 days, program end plus 60 days).
2023-03-01 School A DSO recommends post-completion OPT. 2023-03-10 I-765 filed (inside 30 days of the recommendation).
2023-05-12 BS program end date on the I-20. Degree conferred 2023-05-20. Latest OPT start the student may request: 2023-07-11. Complete-by (14 months): 2024-07-12.
2023-06-19 to 2024-06-18 bachelor's OPT card, 12 months. Unemployed 2023-06-19 to 2023-08-06 (49 days), then employed full time from 2023-08-07.
2024-01-15 admitted to MS Computer Science (STEM-designated) at School B, program start 2024-08-26.
2024-06-18 bachelor's OPT card ends. Grace would end 2024-08-17 (card end plus 60 days).
2024-07-15 School A sets the transfer release date (after the card ended, inside the grace period). School B issues a transfer I-20.
2024-08-26 MS classes begin. Five months after the OPT end is 2024-11-18, so the start is inside it. Last day to contact the School B DSO: 2024-09-10 (15 days after program start).
2026-02-14 to 2026-07-14 MS OPT filing window. 2026-05-15 MS program end date. Complete-by 2027-07-15.
2026-06-15 to 2027-06-14 master's OPT card, a second 12 months. Unemployed 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-31 (47 days), employed from 2026-08-01 with an E-Verify employer.
2027-03-16 STEM extension filing window opens (card end minus 90 days).
Today 2026-09-29: on master's OPT, 47 of 90 unemployment days used on this card.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. A second 12 months only because the level went up: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10), "A student may be authorized 12 months of practical training, and becomes eligible for another 12 months of practical training when they change to a higher educational level." [pack: opt.max_months]. SEVP Help Hub page (saved 2026-09-28): "Twelve months of Regular OPT is available for each higher level of study." Duly must know the level of each program to know which 12-month pool a card draws from.
2. Each program has its own OPT windows, counted from its own program end date: (f)(11)(i)(B)(2) [pack: opt.apply_before_days 90; opt.apply_after_days 60 under ds_2012, 30 under the enjoined 91 FR 44976; opt.file_within_days_of_recommendation 30]; (f)(11)(i)(D) [pack: opt.latest_start_after_days]; (f)(10)(ii)(A)(3) 14 months [pack: opt.complete_within_months].
3. Unemployment is counted per post-completion OPT period: (f)(10)(ii)(E), "during any post-completion OPT period" [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days]. The 49 bachelor's days and the 47 master's days sit against separate limits. SEVP Policy Guidance 1004-03 (2010, saved) 7.1.4: "For each new period of post-completion OPT, the student will have the full 90-day period of unemployment." That the bachelor's days do not carry into the master's count is Duly's reading of the words and must be marked as one.
4. Transfer after OPT: (f)(8)(i), the student "must be able resume classes within 5 months of transferring out of the school that recommended OPT or the date the OPT authorization ends, whichever is earlier"; (f)(8)(ii) release date, and contact with the transfer-in DSO within 15 days of the program start date; (f)(5)(iv) the grace period allows time "to transfer in accordance with paragraph (f)(8)"; (f)(5)(ii) a change of level is maintained through the (f)(8) procedure. (f)(10)(ii)(B) ends OPT when the student transfers, and guidance 1004-03 6.10 says OPT ends on the transfer release date, so a release date before 2024-06-18 would have cut the card short. None of these rules is in the pack.
5. Grace: (f)(5)(iv) [pack: grace.after_completion_days 60 operative, 30 enjoined].
6. STEM next: (f)(10)(ii)(C) and (f)(11)(i)(C) [pack: stem.apply_before_expiry_days, stem.apply_window_closes_rule, stem.requires.*]. The basis may be the MS.
What today's case cannot hold: two programs, two OPT cards, a transfer release date, a program start date. degree_level is one value and the engine only echoes it in the opt.earlier_at_this_level question. Entering the bachelor's card with the master's end date raises opt.ead_end.not_after_program_end and merges the 49 days into the master's count.

journeys.title: STEM extension based on an earlier US STEM bachelor's while on OPT from a non-STEM MBA, inside and outside the 10-year window
journeys.timeline:
2014-08-25 BS Computer Science (STEM-designated) begins at School A, a US school, accredited and SEVP-certified.
2018-05-11 BS program end. Degree conferred 2018-05-19. No OPT used on the BS; the student goes home to work.
2024-08-26 MBA (not STEM-designated) begins at School B.
2025-09-13 to 2026-02-10 MBA OPT filing window. 2025-12-12 MBA program end.
2026-01-20 to 2027-01-19 MBA OPT card, the master's-level 12 months.
2026-10-21 STEM filing window opens (OPT card end minus 90 days).
2026-10-26 Form I-983 signed with an E-Verify employer, software engineer role related to the BS in Computer Science.
2026-11-02 School B DSO (school of most recent enrollment) recommends the 24-month extension on the basis of the BS. I-765 must be filed by 2027-01-01 (60 days after the recommendation) and before the OPT card ends on 2027-01-19.
2026-11-20 STEM I-765 filed.
2027-01-20 to 2029-01-19 STEM card if approved (from the day after the OPT card ends, 24 months, whatever the approval date).
2028-05-19 last day of the 10 years after the BS was conferred. The 2026-11-02 recommendation is inside them.
Variant: BS conferred 2016-05-14. The 10 years end 2026-05-14, before the 2026-11-02 recommendation, so the BS cannot be the basis and the MBA is not STEM: no extension.
Variant: a STEM extension was already used on the BS in 2019 to 2021. A later extension must rest on a higher degree level than the BS, and an MBA on the list would be needed.
Today 2026-09-29: on MBA OPT; the STEM filing window opens in 22 days.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The extension is requested from a valid post-completion OPT period, for the first qualifying degree: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C) opening text [pack: stem.requires_post_completion_opt, stem.extension_months, stem.apply_window_closes_rule].
2. Previously obtained degree: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(3), the degree "must have been conferred from a U.S. educational institution that is accredited and SEVP-certified at the time the student's DSO recommends", must be on the current STEM list at the recommendation, and must be "conferred within the 10 years preceding the date the DSO recommends the student for the 24-month OPT extension" [pack: stem.requires.previously_obtained_degree, a flag; the pack holds no number for the 10 years and no date fact for conferral].
3. The degree: (C)(1) accreditation [pack: stem.requires.accreditation]; (C)(2) a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree in a listed field [pack: stem.requires.dhs_approved_degree, stem.requires.degree_on_designated_list]; (f)(11)(ii)(A) the DSO of most recent enrollment certifies the degree code.
4. The job: (C)(4) directly related to the degree that qualifies, "which may be the previously obtained degree" [pack: stem.requires.eligible_practical_training_opportunity]; (C)(7)(i) and (iii) the I-983 goes to the DSO at the school of most recent enrollment and explains the relation to the qualifying STEM degree [pack: stem.requires.training_plan]; (C)(5) E-Verify [pack: stem.requires.employer_qualification].
5. Filing: (f)(11)(i)(C) up to 90 days before the OPT card expires, within 60 days of the recommendation [pack: stem.apply_before_expiry_days, stem.file_within_days_of_recommendation]; (f)(11)(iii)(A) the extension begins the day after the initial OPT ends.
6. Lifetime: (f)(10)(ii)(C) two extensions at most, and a later one must rest on a higher degree level than the first basis.
What today's case cannot hold: the earlier degree (school, level, field, conferral date, US or not, accredited and SEVP-certified at the recommendation), the degree that is the basis of the extension, any earlier extension. degree_level would read master and nothing would say the basis is a bachelor's.

journeys.title: Second master's at the same level, with OPT split between the two
journeys.timeline:
2022-08-22 MS Management (not STEM) begins at School A.
2023-05-22 to 2023-08-11 full-time CPT, summer internship (82 days).
2023-09-16 to 2024-02-13 OPT filing window for MS 1. 2023-12-15 MS 1 program end.
2023-11-01 DSO recommends post-completion OPT for 6 months only and notes in SEVIS that the student is splitting OPT between two master's programs.
2024-01-22 to 2024-07-21 OPT card, 6 months.
2024-02-10 admitted to MS Business Analytics (STEM-designated) at School B.
2024-07-22 transfer release date from School A, the day after the card ends. Grace would end 2024-09-19. Five months after the OPT end: 2024-12-21.
2024-08-26 MS 2 classes begin at School B.
2025-05-19 to 2025-08-15 full-time CPT (89 days). Full-time CPT at the master's level: 82 + 89 = 171 days.
2026-02-07 to 2026-07-07 OPT filing window for MS 2. 2026-05-08 MS 2 program end.
2026-06-01 to 2026-11-30 OPT card, the remaining 6 months at the master's level.
2026-09-01 STEM filing window opens. Basis: MS 2, the first qualifying degree.
2026-12-01 to 2028-11-30 STEM card if approved.
Variant: MS 1 used all 12 months. Per SEVP no OPT can then be requested for MS 2 at the same level, so there is no OPT period on MS 2 to extend.
Today 2026-09-29: inside the STEM filing window, on the second 6-month card.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. No new 12 months at the same level: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10), 12 months, and another 12 "when they change to a higher educational level" [pack: opt.max_months]. SEVP Help Hub page (saved): a student "can split their OPT time between degree programs at the same education level", and "If you initially request 12 months of OPT based on one degree program, the student will be unable to later request OPT based on a different degree program at the same education level." This is guidance and not in the pack.
2. CPT across two programs at one level: (f)(10)(i), "Students who have received one year or more of full time curricular practical training are ineligible for post-completion academic training" [pack: cpt.full_time_months_bar and cpt.full_time_bar_days, a reading of 365 days]. SEVP page: "Full-time CPT at a previous school at the same program level counts toward the CPT 12month total affecting OPT." 171 is under 365.
3. Unemployment: (f)(10)(ii)(E) per post-completion OPT period [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days]; guidance 1004-03 7.1.4: a student who splits OPT between two degrees at the same level gets the full 90 days for each new period.
4. STEM: (f)(10)(ii)(C) the first qualifying degree, requested from a valid post-completion OPT period [pack: stem.requires_post_completion_opt]. The 81 FR 13040 preamble (saved) says two degrees at the same level do not start a new 12 months.
5. Moving between programs: (f)(8)(i) "transferring between schools or programs", the 5 months; (f)(10)(ii)(B) OPT ends on transfer; (f)(5)(iv) grace.
6. Enjoined (91 FR 44976, 2026-09-15 text, (f)(5)(ii)(C)): "An alien who has completed a program after September 15, 2026, in the United States as an F-1 student at one educational level may not maintain, be admitted, or otherwise be provided F-1 status through a program at the same educational level or a lower educational level." (f)(5)(ii)(A) of that text also bars graduate students from changing objectives. Not operative today, but the pack needs these under the fixed_admission_2026 regime.
What today's case cannot hold: a CPT count per level or per school; two OPT cards at one level; a split noted in SEVIS; the months used at each level.

journeys.title: PhD after a master's: STEM OPT cut short by a transfer, doctoral CPT, a program extension, then a second 12 months and a second STEM extension
journeys.timeline:
2018-08-20 MS Chemistry (STEM-designated) begins at School A.
2020-05-15 MS program end. OPT filing window closed 2020-07-14.
2020-06-22 to 2021-06-21 master's OPT card.
2021-06-22 to 2023-06-21 first STEM card, basis the MS.
2022-02-01 admitted to PhD Chemistry at School B, program start 2022-08-22.
2022-08-15 transfer release date. STEM OPT authorization ends; 310 days of the card go unused. Final I-983 evaluation for the job ending that day due by 2022-08-25.
2022-08-22 PhD begins, inside five months of the release date (2023-01-15).
2024-05-20 to 2024-08-09 full-time CPT, industry internship, counted at the doctoral level only.
2025-05-09 all course requirements done except the dissertation. The student may choose pre-completion OPT (thesis only) or post-completion OPT; the student waits.
2026-04-01 extension requested; 2026-04-10 DSO extends the program end from 2026-05-15 to 2027-05-14 (unexpected research problems).
2027-02-13 to 2027-07-13 doctoral OPT filing window. 2027-05-14 PhD program end. Complete-by 2028-07-14.
Next: doctoral OPT 12 months (higher level), then a second STEM extension based on the PhD, the lifetime maximum of two.
Today 2026-09-29: PhD candidate with program end 2027-05-14.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. OPT ends on transfer or on starting another level: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(B), "Authorization to engage in optional practical training employment is automatically terminated when the student transfers to another school or begins study at another educational level." Guidance 1004-03 6.10: ends on the transfer release date. Not in the pack.
2. Transfer from OPT: (f)(8)(i) classes within 5 months of transferring out or of the OPT end, whichever is earlier; (f)(8)(ii) procedure.
3. Final evaluation when the opportunity ends early: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(i) [pack: stem.evaluation_due_days].
4. A new 12 months at the doctoral level: (f)(10) [pack: opt.max_months]. CPT counted per level: (f)(10)(i) with the SEVP page, "CPT at another program level does not affect OPT" [pack: cpt.full_time_bar_days, a reading].
5. OPT after all course requirements except the thesis: (f)(10)(ii)(A)(3). Pre-completion OPT: (f)(10)(ii)(A)(1) and (2). Guidance 1004-03 6.7: thesis-only pre-completion OPT is not under the unemployment limits and allows a program extension; post-completion OPT allows STEM and cap-gap. Guidance only.
6. Program extension: (f)(7)(i) apply before the program end date; (f)(7)(iii) compelling academic or medical reasons; (f)(7)(iv) new I-20. Not in the pack.
7. Second STEM extension: (f)(10)(ii)(C), a second extension for a degree "at a higher degree level than the first", "In no event may a student be authorized for more than two lifetime STEM OPT extensions", and a 17-month extension counts as one. Not in the pack as a rule.
8. Unemployment for the doctoral OPT and the second extension: (f)(10)(ii)(E) "during a total OPT period" [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days, stem.unemployment_limit_days]. That the master's periods are a separate total OPT period is Duly's reading.
What today's case cannot hold: a STEM card that ended early, a second STEM, a count of lifetime extensions, the level each card belongs to. degree_level would read doctorate and the master's cards would be read against the PhD end date.

journeys.title: Pre-completion OPT full time in summer and part time in term, then post-completion OPT for what remains
journeys.timeline:
2024-08-26 MS Electrical Engineering (STEM-designated) begins at School A.
2025-02-08 earliest filing for pre-completion OPT (90 days before one full academic year).
2025-05-09 one full academic year complete (end of the spring term).
2025-02-20 DSO recommends full-time pre-completion OPT for the summer. 2025-03-05 I-765 filed.
2025-05-19 to 2025-08-15 full-time pre-completion OPT card, school not in session (89 days).
2025-06-25 DSO recommends part-time pre-completion OPT for the fall. 2025-07-10 I-765 filed.
2025-09-02 to 2025-12-19 part-time pre-completion OPT card, at most 20 hours a week in session (109 days).
2026-02-14 to 2026-07-14 post-completion filing window. 2026-02-20 DSO recommends post-completion OPT for the remaining time. 2026-03-02 I-765 filed.
2026-05-15 program end. Complete-by 2027-07-15.
2026-06-08 to 2027-01-14 post-completion card as issued (the end reflects the remaining time).
2026-10-16 STEM filing window opens (card end minus 90 days).
Today 2026-09-29: on post-completion OPT; part of the master's-level 12 months was used before the program ended.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Pre-completion OPT: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(A)(1) during vacation when enrolled and intending to register; (A)(2) "not exceed 20 hours a week while school is in session". Filing: (f)(11)(i)(B)(1), up to 90 days before one full academic year. Not in the pack.
2. One pool of 12 months per level: (f)(10) [pack: opt.max_months]; (f)(11)(iii)(A) post-completion OPT "ends at the conclusion of the remaining time period of post-completion OPT eligibility".
3. How part-time time is deducted: guidance only. Guidance 1004-03 6.6 (2010): "the six months of part-time OPT used by the student would account for three months of the total amount available at that education level". Not in the pack. The register (IMPL-017) keeps the half-time deduction behind a verify gate until it is found in primary text, so Duly takes the card end as printed and does not compute the remaining months.
4. Definitions: SEVP page, pre-completion is "Any portion of OPT used before the student's Program End Date" [pack: opt.post_completion_definition]. SEVIS will not allow overlapping segments.
5. Unemployment counts only in post-completion OPT: (f)(10)(ii)(E) [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days]. SPEC-resolutions point 42: pre-completion days are never counted. Hours: post-completion at least 20 hours a week [pack: opt.min_hours_per_week, guidance].
6. 14 months from the program end: (f)(10)(ii)(A)(3) [pack: opt.complete_within_months]. Then STEM: (f)(11)(i)(C).
What today's case cannot hold: more than one OPT card, a full-time or part-time mark on a card, months used at a level. Entering either pre-completion card raises opt.ead_end.not_after_program_end, and while it is open the post-completion card cannot be entered.

journeys.title: Full-time CPT near one year across co-op terms, with part-time CPT that does not count
journeys.timeline:
2023-08-21 MS Mechanical Engineering (co-op track) begins at School A. The bachelor's was earned abroad, so no US bachelor's CPT exists.
2024-05-09 one full academic year complete.
2024-05-20 to 2024-08-16 full-time CPT, Employer X (89 days; running total 89).
2024-08-19 to 2024-12-20 full-time CPT co-op, Employer X (124 days; running 213).
2025-01-06 to 2025-05-16 full-time CPT co-op, Employer Y (131 days; running 344).
Planning point: a further full-time CPT of 20 days (2025-05-19 to 2025-06-07) gives 364. 21 days (to 2025-06-08) gives 365, Duly's count of one year.
2025-05-19 to 2025-06-13 full-time CPT actually taken (26 days; running 370).
2025-08-25 to 2025-12-12 part-time CPT, 20 hours a week (not added to the full-time total).
2025-09-13 to 2026-02-10 OPT filing window. 2025-12-12 program end.
Variant: the same 344 days entered with a leap day inside a period. A year counted as 366 days, or as 12 calendar months, gives a different edge than 365.
Variant: full-time CPT at an earlier US bachelor's level does not count toward this master's total.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The bar: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(i), "Students who have received one year or more of full time curricular practical training are ineligible for post-completion academic training." [pack: cpt.full_time_months_bar 12, cpt.full_time_bar_days 365; both marked as readings]. The engine gives the judgement item cpt_full_time_at_or_over_bar at 365 or more, so the answer goes to the DSO.
2. What counts: only periods the DSO marked full time in SEVIS. (f)(10)(i): "The DSO will indicate whether the training is full-time or part-time, the employer and location, and the employment start and end date." CPT may begin only after the endorsed I-20.
3. Level and school: SEVP page (saved), "Full-time CPT at a previous school at the same program level counts toward the CPT 12month total affecting OPT. CPT at another program level does not affect OPT."
4. The one-academic-year condition, and its exception: (f)(10) and (f)(10)(i), "Exceptions to the one academic year requirement are provided for students enrolled in graduate studies that require immediate participation in curricular practical training."
5. Counting method: inclusive days, days between periods not counted, overlapping periods counted once, 365 rather than 366 or 12 calendar months. Each is Duly's reading of "one year" and must be marked as one.
What today's case cannot hold: CPT periods. It holds a single integer, cpt_full_time_days, with no dates, no full-time or part-time mark, no employer, no level and no school. It cannot sum periods, split by level, or show the planning point.

journeys.title: Transfer between schools mid-bachelor's, with a summer abroad and CPT at both schools
journeys.timeline:
2023-08-21 BS Computer Science begins at School A.
2024-05-20 to 2024-08-09 full-time CPT at School A (82 days).
2024-09-03 on-campus job at School A, 20 hours a week in session.
2025-02-15 admitted to BS Computer Science at School B as a transfer, start 2025-08-25.
2025-03-01 student tells School A of the intent to transfer. School A DSO sets release date 2025-05-09 (end of the spring term).
2025-05-09 release date. The on-campus job at School A ends. School B gets the SEVIS record and issues a transfer I-20.
2025-06-01 to 2025-08-15 summer at home. Re-entry with School B's transfer I-20.
2025-08-25 classes begin at School B, inside five months of the release date (2025-10-09).
2025-09-09 last day to contact the School B DSO (15 days after program start).
2026-05-18 to 2026-08-07 full-time CPT at School B. The same-level total includes School A's 82 days.
2027-02-13 to 2027-07-13 OPT filing window. 2027-05-14 BS program end at School B.
Today 2026-09-29: senior at School B.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Who may transfer and when: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(8)(i), a student maintaining status may transfer; classes must begin "within five months of transferring out of the current school or within 5 months of the program completion date on their current Form I-20 or successor form, whichever is earlier"; a student not pursuing a full course at the last school must seek reinstatement under (f)(16).
2. Procedure: (f)(8)(ii) notice to the transfer-out school, release date, cancellation only before the release date, contact with the transfer-in DSO within 15 days of the program start date, transfer complete when enrolled "in accordance with the 30 days required by § 214.3(g)(2)(iii)". 8 CFR 214.3 is not saved in the pack.
3. On-campus work: (f)(9)(i), "In the case of a transfer in SEVIS, the student may only engage in on-campus employment at the school having jurisdiction over the student's SEVIS record."
4. Travel: (f)(4)(ii) an updated I-20 when the student "intends to transfer"; (f)(5)(iii) annual vacation.
5. Practical training: (f)(10) one full academic year of full-time enrollment. Whether School A's year counts at School B is not stated in the saved words, so it is a DSO question. CPT at School A counts toward the same-level total (SEVP page). (f)(10)(ii)(B) ends any OPT on transfer. (f)(13)(i) an off-campus authorization on the I-20 resumes only at the same school.
None of these rules is in the pack.
What today's case cannot hold: a school history, a release date, a program start date, a transfer I-20, or CPT by school. The case has school only as one optional id in the generic contract.

journeys.title: Change of educational level at the same school while on OPT: bachelor's OPT ends when the master's begins
journeys.timeline:
2020-08-24 BS Mathematics (STEM-designated) begins at School A.
2024-02-10 to 2024-07-09 BS OPT filing window. 2024-05-10 BS program end.
2024-06-03 to 2025-06-02 bachelor's OPT card. Unemployed 2024-06-03 to 2024-07-07 (35 days); employed from 2024-07-08.
2024-10-15 admitted to MS Statistics at School A, start 2025-01-13. School A issues a new I-20 at the master's level.
2025-01-13 MS classes begin. The bachelor's OPT ends: 224 days of the card used (2024-06-03 to 2025-01-12), 141 days left unused and not carried to the master's level.
2025-01-13 on-campus research assistantship under the new I-20.
2026-09-19 to 2027-02-16 MS OPT filing window. 2026-12-18 MS program end. Complete-by 2028-02-18.
Next: a new 12 months of OPT at the master's level; a STEM extension on the MS Statistics or on the BS Mathematics (conferred 2024, inside 10 years).
Today 2026-09-29: the MS OPT filing window is open.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Change of level: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii), a student "who continues from one educational level to another is considered to be maintaining status, provided that the transition to the new educational level is accomplished according to transfer procedures outlined in paragraph (f)(8)".
2. OPT ends: (f)(10)(ii)(B), terminated when the student "begins study at another educational level". Guidance 1004-03 6.10 says OPT ends on the transfer release date for a change of education level at the same school. The two sources can give different days; Duly shows both and asks the DSO.
3. Timing from OPT: (f)(8)(i), within 5 months of transferring out or of the OPT end, whichever is earlier.
4. New 12 months: (f)(10) [pack: opt.max_months]; unused bachelor's months are not carried (SEVP page, 12 months per higher level).
5. Travel: (f)(4)(ii) an updated I-20 for a student "who has advanced to a higher level of study". Work: (f)(9)(i), a student issued an I-20 for a new program under § 214.3(k) may continue on-campus work (8 CFR 214.3 not saved).
6. STEM basis choices: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(3) [pack: stem.requires.previously_obtained_degree].
7. Enjoined 2026-09-15 text: (f)(5)(ii)(B) keeps status for a new, higher program; (f)(5)(ii)(A) bars graduate students from changing objectives during a program. Not operative today.
What today's case cannot hold: a card that ended early because of a change of level, the date the master's began, a second program end. Entering the bachelor's card against the MS end date raises opt.ead_end.not_after_program_end, and unemployment would keep counting after the card was ended.

journeys.title: Program extension asked for in time, with OPT windows that move, and the late request that cannot be granted

2025-02-15 to 2025-07-15 OPT filing window under the old end date.
2025-03-10 advisor confirms the thesis is delayed by an equipment failure (unexpected research problems).

2025-04-28 DSO grants it in SEVIS. New I-20 program end 2025-12-19.
2025-09-20 to 2026-02-17 OPT filing window under the new end date. Latest start 2026-02-17. Complete-by 2027-02-19. Grace, if no OPT, to 2026-02-17.

2026-01-12 to 2027-01-11 OPT card.
Variant (late): the request is made on 2025-05-20, after the old end date. The DSO may not grant it; the student is out of status and may seek reinstatement, filed within 5 months of being out of status. Duly does not date when status ended; that is for the DSO.

journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. When to ask: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(7)(i), must apply "prior to the program end date"; (f)(7)(iii), "A DSO may not grant an extension if the student did not apply for an extension until after the program end date"; a student who cannot finish and is not eligible "is considered out of status".
2. Reasons: (f)(7)(iii), compelling academic or medical reasons, "such as changes of major or research topics, unexpected research problems, or documented illnesses"; "Delays caused by academic probation or suspension are not acceptable reasons".
3. How: (f)(7)(iv), only by updating SEVIS and issuing a new I-20; (f)(6)(iii)(E) the same when a reduced course load needs a later end date.
4. Out of status: (f)(16)(i)(A), not out of status for more than 5 months at filing.
5. OPT windows count from the program end date in force [pack: opt.apply_before_days, opt.apply_after_days, opt.latest_start_after_days, opt.complete_within_months]. Guidance 1004-03 6.7: thesis-only pre-completion OPT allows a program extension; post-completion OPT does not.
No extension rule is in the pack.
What today's case cannot hold: a history of program end dates, the date an extension was asked for and granted. The engine holds one program_end_date, so an OPT filing made under the old date would be checked against the new one, and nothing can check that the request came before the old end date.

journeys.title: A gap between two programs: inside five months, past five months, and at the same school
journeys.timeline:
2023-08-21 MS Physics begins at School A.
2025-05-16 MS program end. No OPT requested.
2025-07-15 grace ends (60 days).
2025-10-16 five months after the program completion date.
Case A (fits the words): admitted to PhD Physics at School B, start 2025-08-25. Transfer release date 2025-06-30, set inside the grace period. Classes begin inside five months. Contact with the School B DSO by 2025-09-09.
Case B (does not fit): the PhD at School B starts 2026-01-12, after 2025-10-16. The words say the student is not permitted to remain in the US while transferring; the student would leave and return with an initial I-20, a matter for the DSO.
Case C (same school): PhD at School A starts 2025-08-25, a change of level. The on-campus job may continue under the new-program I-20.
Summer 2025: the student is not continuing in the same program; whether the annual vacation rule applies is a reading, for the DSO.
Variant with OPT: had OPT been used, classes must begin within 5 months of transferring out or of the OPT end, whichever is earlier.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Grace: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(iv), a student who has completed a course of study has an additional 60 days "to prepare for departure from the United States or to transfer in accordance with paragraph (f)(8)" [pack: grace.after_completion_days 60 operative; the enjoined text (f)(5)(v) gives 30].
2. The five months: (f)(8)(i), "not permitted to remain in the United States when transferring between schools or programs unless the student will begin classes at the transfer school or program within five months of transferring out of the current school or within 5 months of the program completion date on their current Form I-20 or successor form, whichever is earlier". Counting five months as calendar months is Duly's reading. Not in the pack.
3. Procedure: (f)(8)(ii), release date and the 15 days.
4. Vacation: (f)(5)(iii) is for a student "eligible and intends to register for the next term".
5. Work: (f)(9)(i), a student with an I-20 for a new program under § 214.3(k) "who intends to enroll for the next regular academic year, term, or session at the institution that issued the Form I-20" may continue on-campus work; otherwise no on-campus work after completing a course of study.
6. Travel in the gap: (f)(4)(ii), an updated I-20 when the student intends to transfer or has advanced to a higher level.
7. Enjoined 2026-09-15 text: a 30-day period, and the bar on a program at the same or a lower level after completing one.
What today's case cannot hold: a next program, a program start date, a release date. The engine shows grace.ends as the end of the record and cannot see that a transfer continues status.

Variant: travel while the OPT I-765 is pending after the program end. No saved source covers it.
Variant: an absence from 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-15 passes five months on 2026-09-01.
Today 2026-09-29: the card ends tomorrow; grace to 2026-11-29.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Re-entry on post-completion OPT: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(13)(ii), a student with an unexpired post-completion EAD "who is otherwise admissible may return to the United States to resume employment after a period of temporary absence", with an I-20 "endorsed for reentry by the DSO within the last six months". Counting six months back from the re-entry day is Duly's reading. Whether a student with no job may re-enter is not in the saved words; the register (IMPL-046) has the assistant step back on "Can I re-enter unemployed?".
2. Length of absence: (f)(4), readmission after "a temporary absence of five months or less"; (f)(4)(ii) an updated I-20 on a substantive change.
3. Days abroad and the count: guidance 1004-03 7.1.8, "Time spent outside the United States during an approved period of post-completion OPT counts as unemployment against the 90/120-day limits, unless the student is either: Employed during a period of leave authorized by an employer; or Traveling as part of his or her employment." The guidance is from 2010; the 120 was replaced by 150 in 2016. Limit: (f)(10)(ii)(E) [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days].
4. Reporting: (f)(12)(i) interruption of employment [pack: opt.report_interruption; opt.report_employer_within_days, guidance].
5. Other travel: STEM travel and cap-gap travel are in the 81 FR 13040 preamble (see J12). Travel with a pending post-completion I-765 is in no saved source, so Duly does not have that rule.
None of the travel rules is in the pack.
What today's case cannot hold: departure and re-entry dates, travel signature dates, a leave marker on an employment period. The count cannot add days abroad or leave out paid leave.

journeys.title: Cap-gap with the H-1B petition approved
journeys.timeline:

2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31 OPT card, employed full time.
2026-03-31 employer's H-1B registration selected.
2026-04-01 cap-subject H-1B petition filed while the OPT card is valid. It asks for a change of status and a start date of 2026-10-01, in fiscal year 2027.
2026-05-31 OPT card ends. From 2026-06-01 status and work authorization are extended automatically.
2026-06-20 petition and change of status approved, validity start 2026-10-01.
2026-07-10 DSO issues an I-20 showing the cap-gap extension.
Cap-gap end: the earlier of April 1 of fiscal year 2027 (2027-04-01) and the approved validity start (2026-10-01). The extension runs until 2026-10-01, when H-1B status begins.
Variant (travel): abroad 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-25. Readmission in F-1 is possible if the petition and change of status are approved, re-entry is before the H-1B start, and the student is otherwise admissible. Travel while the petition is pending leads USCIS to deem it abandoned.
Variant (pending): still pending on 2026-10-01. Under the rule for petitions filed from 2025-01-17, the extension runs to 2027-04-01 or the approved validity start, whichever is earlier.
Variant (old rule): a petition filed before 2025-01-17 is read with the October 1 row.
Today 2026-09-29: two days before the H-1B start.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The extension: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi)(A), status and employment authorization under 274a.12(c)(3)(i)(B) or (C) extended "until April 1 of the fiscal year for which such H-1B status is being requested or until the validity start date of the approved petition, whichever is earlier", for a petition that (1) "Has been timely filed", (2) asks for a start in that fiscal year, (3) "Is nonfrivolous" [pack: capgap.end_month_day 04-01, and 10-01 for earlier petitions; capgap.fiscal_year_start_month_day from 31 U.S.C. 1102; capgap.october_start_condition].
2. The student must not have violated status: (f)(5)(vi)(C). F-2 dependents are covered: (f)(5)(vi)(D).
3. Employment during cap-gap: 274a.12(b)(6)(v), in the 81 FR 13040 amendment text (saved). The current 274a.12 is not saved.
4. Travel: 81 FR 13040 preamble (saved). Readmission during a cap-gap period if "(1) The student's H-1B petition and request for change of status has been approved; (2) the student seeks readmission before his or her H-1B employment begins" and (3) the student is otherwise admissible; travel before approval and "USCIS will deem the petition abandoned".
5. Unemployment keeps counting in cap-gap: guidance 1004-03 9.4.3, "the 90 day limitation on unemployment continues during the cap gap extension" (2010 guidance) [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days].
6. A petition filed after the card has ended: the words extend "any employment authorization granted". With no card left, Duly reads that no work authorization is extended, and marks it as a reading.
What today's case holds: petition_filed_on, requested_start, change_of_status, status. It cannot hold: the approval date, the approved validity start (the engine uses the requested start in its place), a receipt date, or travel. If the approval gives another validity start, the engine's end date is wrong.

journeys.title: Cap-gap with the H-1B petition denied, plus the rejected and still-pending-on-April-1 variants
journeys.timeline:

2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 OPT card, employed full time.
2026-04-01 petition filed while the card is valid. It asks for a change of status and a start of 2026-10-01.
2026-07-01 cap-gap begins.
2026-08-14 petition denied. The automatic extension ends that day and work stops.
2026-10-13 sixty days after the denial. The 89 FR 103054 preamble says such a student would "generally" get the standard 60-day grace period "consistent with existing USCIS practice". That is preamble, not regulation text.
Variant (rejected): petition rejected 2026-04-20 as not properly filed. No extension; the card ends 2026-06-30 and grace runs to 2026-08-29.
Variant (pending on April 1): pending through 2027-04-01. Per the preamble, OPT authorization ends and the 60-day grace period begins on April 1, ending 2027-05-31.
Variant (denied while the card is valid): denial on 2026-05-20. The card runs to 2026-06-30 and grace is counted from the card end.
Today 2026-09-29: inside the 60 days after the denial, if the preamble's practice applies.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. What ends the extension: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi)(B), it "shall automatically terminate upon the rejection, denial, revocation, or withdrawal of the H-1B petition" or upon the denial or withdrawal of the change-of-status request.
2. The grace period after a denial: the regulation text does not say. 89 FR 103054 preamble (saved): "would generally receive the standard F-1 grace period of 60 days", and "If the H-1B petition is still pending on April 1, then the beneficiary of the petition is no longer authorized for OPT and the 60-day grace period begins on April 1." DHS "declines add this language to the regulatory text." Guidance 1004-03 (2010) has a table row saying the grace period ends 60 days after a withdrawal or denial. Neither is in the pack. Any row Duly adds is preamble or guidance and is marked so.
3. Grace in general: (f)(5)(iv) [pack: grace.after_completion_days].
4. The extension itself: (f)(5)(vi)(A) [pack: capgap.end_month_day].
What today's case cannot hold: a denial date. The engine sees status denied, gives the judgement item cap_gap_petition_not_active, and counts grace.ends from the card end (2026-08-29). That is earlier than the date the preamble describes. So Duly must hold the denial date and step back to the DSO instead of stating the card-end grace date.

2026-06-01 cap-gap extends the STEM employment authorization.

2026-07-25 Employer Z withdraws the petition. The automatic extension ends.
Grace after a withdrawal: no saved rule text gives it. Sixty days would be 2026-09-23, but Duly states no date and asks the DSO.
Variant (consular): on 2026-07-01 Employer Z asks for consular processing instead of a change of status. The petition is later approved. The extension ends when the change of status is withdrawn.

journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The extension covers STEM authorization: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi)(A), "any employment authorization granted under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(3)(i)(B) or (C)".
2. Withdrawal and consular processing: (f)(5)(vi)(B), terminates on withdrawal of the petition or on withdrawal of the change-of-status request, "even if the H-1B petition filed on the F-1 student's behalf is approved for consular processing".
3. Grace after withdrawal: the 89 FR 103054 preamble speaks of a petition that "is denied"; nothing saved speaks to a withdrawal. Duly does not have this rule and says so.
4. Reporting and the evaluation: (f)(12)(ii)(A), within 10 days a "loss of employment" [pack: stem.report_change_within_days]; (f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(i) final evaluation within 10 days of the conclusion of the opportunity [pack: stem.evaluation_due_days]; (f)(10)(ii)(C)(6) the employer reports the end within five business days [pack: stem.requires.employer_reporting].
5. Count: (f)(10)(ii)(E), 150 "during a total OPT period" [pack: stem.unemployment_limit_days]. That cap-gap days are in the total is Duly's reading, supported by guidance 1004-03 9.4.3.
What today's case cannot hold: the date a petition was withdrawn, revoked or denied (the status enum has the values but no dates), or a change of status withdrawn while the petition stands. The engine cannot place the day the extension ended, so it cannot end the count or the work authorization on the right day.

journeys.title: Unemployment counted across OPT and STEM OPT, with the 180-day extension, a change of employer, and weeks under 20 hours
journeys.timeline:

2024-06-15 to 2025-06-14 OPT card.

2024-08-20 to 2025-03-31 Job A, 40 hours a week.
2025-04-01 to 2025-04-20 unemployed (20 days). OPT card total: 86 of 90.
2025-04-21 Job B, E-Verify employer, 40 hours a week.
2025-03-16 STEM window opens. 2025-04-25 DSO recommends. 2025-05-02 STEM I-765 filed.
2025-06-14 OPT card ends while the STEM application is pending. Work continues under the automatic extension, up to 180 days (no later than 2025-12-11).
2025-07-20 STEM approved. STEM card 2025-06-15 to 2027-06-14, whatever the approval date.
2025-10-31 last day at Job B. Loss of employment report and Job B final evaluation due 2025-11-10.
2025-11-01 to 2025-11-30 unemployed (30 days).
2025-12-01 Job C, a new E-Verify employer. New I-983 due 2025-12-11.
2025-12-30 validation report 1 due (2025-12-15 plus 10 business days, Christmas skipped).
2026-01-05 to 2026-01-25 Job C at 15 hours a week (21 days under 20 hours). 2026-01-26 back to 40 hours; modified I-983.

journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. Limits: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E), 90 "during any post-completion OPT period" and 150 "during a total OPT period, including any post-completion OPT period ... and any subsequent 24-month extension period" [pack: opt.unemployment_limit_days, stem.unemployment_limit_days]. SPEC-resolutions point 19: the OPT card keeps its own 90.
2. Hours: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(8), not "less than 20 hours per week" [pack: stem.min_hours_per_week]; SEVP page, post-completion OPT "must be at least 20 hours per week or full-time" [pack: opt.min_hours_per_week, guidance]; "A student whose record lacks employer information is considered unemployed." Whether days under 20 hours count as unemployment is Duly's reading.
3. When the count starts: guidance 1004-03 7.1.6, OPT authorization begins on the start date on the EAD, so days before the card are not counted.
4. The pending STEM application: (f)(11)(i)(C) and 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) as written in 81 FR 13040 (saved), "not to exceed 180 days". The current 274a.12 is not saved, and the register (IMPL-017) gates the 180 days until it is pulled from primary text. (f)(11)(iii)(A): the extension "begins on the day after the expiration of the initial post-completion OPT employment authorization and ends 24 months thereafter, regardless of the date the actual extension is approved".
5. STEM duties: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(7)(iv) new I-983 within 10 days [pack: stem.new_plan_due_days]; (C)(9)(ii) modified I-983 for a significant cut in hours; (f)(12)(ii)(A) and (B) [pack: stem.report_change_within_days, stem.validation_interval_months, stem.validation_due_business_days, calendar.federal_holidays_law]; (C)(9)(i) [pack: stem.evaluation_interval_months, stem.evaluation_due_days].
What today's case holds: one OPT card, one STEM card, employment periods with hours. This is the part the engine already counts. It cannot hold: the 180-day period as a fact, employer identity (it asks employment.<n>.new_employer), a change of hours inside one period (the period must be split), or days abroad.

journeys.timeline:

2024-08-26 MBA (not STEM-designated) begins at School A. First US program; I-20 level: master's.

2026-01-12 back in the US for the final term, on an I-20 endorsed for travel.

journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The first year: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10), one full academic year of full-time enrollment in an SEVP-certified college or university. The study-abroad sentence: it "also includes students who, during their course of study, were enrolled in a study abroad program, if the student had spent at least one full academic term enrolled in a full course of study in the United States prior to studying abroad". CPT before a full year only for "graduate studies that require immediate participation" ((f)(10)(i)).
2. No STEM on a foreign degree: (f)(10)(ii)(C)(1), "from a U.S. educational institution accredited" [pack: stem.requires.accreditation]; (C)(3), a previously obtained degree "conferred from a U.S. educational institution that is accredited and SEVP-certified" [pack: stem.requires.previously_obtained_degree]; 81 FR 13040 preamble (saved): "Overseas campuses of U.S. educational institutions are not eligible for SEVP certification."
3. Twelve months at the first US level: (f)(10) [pack: opt.max_months].
4. Travel back for the final term: (f)(4)(i).
5. Enjoined 2026-09-15 text (f)(5)(ii)(C) speaks of a program completed "in the United States as an F-1 student"; a foreign degree is outside it.
What today's case cannot hold: a degree marked foreign, a study-abroad term, the field of a degree. When the path model asks for a STEM basis, nothing tells a foreign STEM degree from a US one. The one-level case would show the extension step next from the OPT card, with only the regulation's list beside it.

journeys.title: Online-course limit across undergraduate terms, and a final term whose one needed class is online
journeys.timeline:
2023-08-21 BS Business Administration begins at School A (semesters).
Fall 2024 (2024-08-26 to 2024-12-13): 15 credits, one online class (3). 15 credits count.
Spring 2025 (2025-01-13 to 2025-05-09): 12 credits, two in-person classes (6) and two online classes (6). Only one online class counts: 6 + 3 = 9 counted, under 12. There was no reduced-course-load approval before the term.
Summer 2025: two online classes during the annual vacation, when no full course is required.
Fall 2025: 15 credits, four in-person classes (12) and one online class (3). 15 count.
Spring 2026: 12 credits in person.
Fall 2026 (2026-08-24 to 2026-12-18): final term, one 3-credit class needed. The DSO approves a final-term reduced course load before 2026-08-24. The only class left is offered online. The saved words do not settle whether one online class can be the whole final-term load.
2026-09-19 to 2027-02-16 OPT filing window. 2026-12-18 program end.
Variant: a term in an English language program. No online class counts at all.
Variant: a graduate student. The full course is what the DSO certifies, and the limit of one online class or 3 credits per term still applies.
Today 2026-09-29: in the final term; the OPT filing window is open.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The limit: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(6)(i)(G), "no more than the equivalent of one class or three credits per session, term, semester, trimester, or quarter may be counted toward the full course of study requirement if the class is taken on-line or through distance education and does not require the student's physical attendance"; in a language study program "no on-line or distance education classes may be considered to count".
2. Full course: (f)(6)(i)(B), undergraduate "at least 12 semester or quarter hours"; (f)(6)(i)(A), graduate study "certified by a DSO as a full course of study". The regulation states no graduate credit number, so that number is school policy (D3), recorded per school with its source.
3. Dropping below: (f)(6)(iii), "A student who drops below a full course of study without the prior approval of the DSO will be considered out of status"; (f)(6)(iii)(C), final term; (f)(16)(i)(F)(2), reinstatement for a reduction "that would have been within a DSO's power to authorize".
4. Vacation: (f)(5)(iii).
None of these rules is in the pack.
What today's case cannot hold: terms, credits, class mode, or any enrollment fact. Duly cannot see a term like Spring 2025 at all. When it can, the question is asked, never answered: "Were two of your classes online that term?".

journeys.title: Reduced course load: academic difficulty once, medical twice toward the 12-month aggregate, a program extension, and an unapproved drop
journeys.timeline:
2024-08-26 BS Biology begins at School A. I-20 program end 2027-05-14.
2024-09-03 DSO approves a reduced course load for initial difficulty with English and updates SEVIS before the drop. Fall 2024 at 6 credits.
2025-01-13 full course resumed in Spring 2025, the next term that is not summer. The DSO reports it by 2025-02-03 (21 days).
Fall 2025: a second reduced load for academic difficulty is asked for and cannot be given at this program level.
2026-01-12 to 2026-05-08 medical reduced load, zero credits, with a letter from a licensed psychologist (117 days).
2026-08-20 DSO extends the program end to 2027-12-17 because of the reduced terms. New I-20.
2026-08-24 to 2026-12-18 medical reduced load, approved again for the term with new documentation (117 days). Aggregate 234 days, about 7.7 of the 12 months at the bachelor's level.
2027-01-11 full course resumes.
Variant: on 2025-10-01 the student drops to 6 credits without prior DSO approval. The student is out of status, and reinstatement may rest on a reduction the DSO could have approved.
Today 2026-09-29: in the second medical term.
journeys.rules_that_decide:
1. The floor and prior approval: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(6)(iii), "at least six semester or quarter hours, or half the clock hours required for a full course of study"; dropping without prior approval is out of status.
2. Academic difficulty: (f)(6)(iii)(A), resume "at the next available term, session, or semester, excluding a summer session"; "not eligible for a second authorization by the DSO due to academic difficulties while pursuing a course of study at that program level".
3. Medical: (f)(6)(iii)(B), "(or, if necessary, no course load)", "not to exceed an aggregate of 12 months while the student is pursuing a course of study at a particular program level"; documentation from a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, psychologist or clinical psychologist; approved again "each new term, session, or semester". Counting the 12 months in days or in months is Duly's reading.
4. Reporting and the extension: (f)(6)(iii)(E), SEVIS updated before the drop, notice within 21 days of resuming, a new I-20 under (f)(7) when the end date moves.
5. Reinstatement: (f)(16)(i)(A) and (F)(2).
6. Practical training: (f)(10) requires one full academic year "lawfully enrolled on a full-time basis". How reduced terms count is not in the saved words, so it is a DSO question.
None of these rules is in the pack.
What today's case cannot hold: terms, reduced-load approvals, reasons, the aggregate per level, or the history of the program end date.

journeys.title: English language program, then an associate's at a community college, then a bachelor's with OPT and STEM OPT

## 11. What Duly works out from the links (L-engine, L-content)

Duly computes these from facts. It never asks the student for them.

- The level of a card, a job or a CPT is its program's `level`.
- Same level means the same `level` value, at any school. "Higher level" follows the pack's order of levels (section 13, point 2). That order is Duly's reading, and it is marked so. Secondary, language_training, professional and other have no place in the order. A comparison with one of them is unknown, and the DSO is asked.
- The end date in force on a day is the program's `end_date`, moved back through its end_date_change records.
- An OPT or STEM authorization ends at card_end, or earlier when a move leaves its program:
  - The regulation ends it when the student "transfers to another school or begins study at another educational level". For a change of level, that is the day before the new program starts. For a transfer, the words name no day. Duly reads it as the release date, and marks that as a reading.
  - SEVP's guidance ends it on the release date.
  - When the two give different days, Duly shows both with their sources. It leaves the items that use the end null and raises the judgement item `<stage>.end_by_source.<record>` (talk_to_dso).
- The school that holds the SEVIS record is the from-program's school until the release date, and the to-program's school after it.
- A total OPT period is one post-completion OPT authorization plus each STEM authorization that extends it.
- A new employer on a STEM card is a work record under it whose employer differs from the one before. The question `employment.<n>.new_employer` is asked only when the employer is not entered.
- A job ends only at a work record's `end`. A change of hours is not an end. It gives no concluding evaluation and no report that a job ended.
- A job's permission is its `under` link, or `on_campus`. A job on campus is never counted as OPT work.
- Days abroad come from trip records.

## 12. A list is whole only when the student says so

The case holds `complete`: the student's statement that a list is whole, with its day. The key is a kind ("program"), or a kind plus the record its items link to ("authorization:p2" means every authorization for program p2).

- Until a list that a shown item or the verdict uses is stated whole, the verdict is cannot_tell with `unconfirmed:complete.<key>`, and a question asks for the statement.
- For work, trip, report and move, a statement covers the days through its own day. A trip statement also holds `from`, the day the list starts. On a later day the question opens again for the days since (product-1 point 3).
- For a records case, this replaces D41's question and product-1 point 39. The student lists every program and card, and Duly counts. It does not guess from one card. The translation keeps both question ids (section 19).
- A new check for every pack is `record.ends_before_today`. When today is after the end of every span in the record, and no later record exists, Duly asks: "Your record ends on <date>. Is there anything after it to add?" Until that is answered, the verdict is cannot_tell. "Nothing after it" gives talk_to_dso with the judgement item, and Duly says nothing about what it means (J04, J09, J10, J13).

## 13. What a pack can say about records (contracts)

The engine stays a reader. No kind, field, choice value or rule of any pack is written in engine/path.py. Everything below is in contracts/rulepack.schema.json (Part 2).

1. **Record kinds.** `path.records` declares each kind: its id prefix, how many records it may have, whether its list grows with time, and its fields. A field has a kind (date, count, number, flag, choice, text, link, periods) and a label. Where they apply, it also has choices, whether "not sure" is an answer, the kinds a link may name, a pattern, `happened`, `school`, `translation_only` and `history`.
2. **An order.** `path.order` lists one field's choices from lowest to highest, with the rules that support the order. A comparison with a value that is not in the list is unknown.
3. **A stage for each record.** A stage with `for_each` is entered once for each record that matches. Its instance id is `<stage id>.<record id>`. Every item, question and conflict it raises ends its id with the record id and carries `record` in the output.
4. **Paths.**
   - A `when` or a condition may read `this.<field>`, or follow up to two links, as in `this.program.end_date`.
   - Inside a selector, `outer` names the record of the stage, check or counter that uses it.
   - `first` takes the earliest or latest date of a field over the records a selector finds.
   - `today` is the person's calendar day.
5. **Conditions.** There is a closed list: in, present, on_or_before, on_or_after, before, after, level_above, level_same, level_below, same_as, differs_from, month_day_is, at_most, exists, none, count_below, count_at_most, any_of, all_of, not. Each reads fields and rule amounts, never a literal number.
6. **Three answers.** A condition is true, false or unknown. It is unknown when a field it reads is absent or "not sure".
   - A missing field is asked, and the verdict is cannot_tell until it is answered.
   - "Not sure" gives the judgement item `<record id>.<field>.not_sure` (talk_to_dso).
   - A step whose condition is unknown is never shown as if it were open, and never hidden as if it were closed. Its dates are shown with the line "Whether this step is open to you is a question for your DSO."
7. **Next, with conditions.** A `next` entry may carry `only_if` and `bind`. The next stage's windows are computed for a record not yet entered, and `bind` sets that record's fields from this one: an OPT for this program, or a STEM extension of this OPT.
8. **A second source for an end.** `span.ends_also` holds other readings of a span's end, each with its rules. When they differ, section 11 applies.
9. **More kinds of date.**
   - In earliest_of and latest_of, a member marked `optional` is skipped when its fact is absent. Any other absent member makes the date missing.
   - `as_of` reads a field with history as it stood on a given day.
   - `in_fiscal_year_of` places a month and day in the fiscal year that holds a date. The fiscal year's first day comes from a rule (J12).
   - `day_before` and `day_after` move a date by one calendar day. They are not amounts (J08, J15).
10. **Checks.** `path.checks` declares each check on the student's own dates and answers: a condition that should hold, the rules behind it, and when it applies.
    - When it does not hold, it works like a conflict in product-1 section 1. The question is "Are these the dates on your documents?", and a yes gives talk_to_dso with the judgement item.
    - A check marked `judgement` goes to the DSO at once.
    - This is how every "within N days or months" rule on a person's dates is checked. Duly never says a step was late.
11. **Counters.** There are four calculators. Each runs over a `scope`: the records it counts, grouped by record, by chain (a record and those that link to it), by a shared value such as a level, or all together.
    - `days_without_qualifying_period` is today's unemployment count, over each group's span. A day counts unless a qualifying record covers it. Days of a `not_qualifying` record count even when covered.
    - `sum_of_days` counts calendar days of the matching spans, first and last day included, each day once where spans overlap.
    - `sum_of_months` measures each span as whole months from its start plus days, then adds them up. The total is over a limit when its months pass the limit, or equal it with days left over.
    - `count_of_records` counts records.

    Each counter names a limit rule. At or over the limit, the verdict carries `<counter>.at_or_over_limit.<group>` (talk_to_dso). How days and months are counted is Duly's reading, and the item says so. `days_in_status` and `count_of_facts` leave the contract, because nothing defines them.
12. **Years.** The unit list gains `years`, for "within the 10 years preceding" (J02). Adding years moves the calendar date, and 29 February becomes 28 February, as month ends do today. That is a reading.
13. **Where a start date comes from.** A rule row gains `effective_from_basis`: `stated`, or `earliest_saved_copy` when the start is only the date of the oldest saved copy. For such a row, an event before that day gives `rule_copy_not_saved_for_event_day`: "Duly has no saved copy of this rule from before <date>. The question is for your DSO." Duly never says the rule was not yet in force (J01, J04, J06, J07, J14, J15).

## 17. What Duly asks, and never assumes

Duly asks for these:

1. That each list is whole (section 12).
2. Each program's level, as the I-20 shows it. It is never read from a degree's name, and it has no default.
3. Whether a degree is on the STEM Designated Degree Program List. It is never read from a major or a CIP code, because the list is not saved.
4. Whether a program is finished, and the days coursework was done and the degree was conferred.
5. Which program each authorization rests on. The form proposes the one whose dates fit, and the student confirms.
6. Whether an OPT card falls before or after the program end, and whether it is full or part time, as the I-20 shows. Duly then checks this against the dates.
7. Full or part time for each CPT, as the DSO marked it.
8. Which degree a STEM extension rests on.
9. Which permission each job was under, and whether a job is on campus.
10. What each trip abroad was: job travel, approved leave, personal, or a study abroad term.
11. Whether an employer is in E-Verify.
12. How the student moved from one program to the next.
13. Whether a petition is under the yearly cap, and each outcome with its day.
14. When the first full academic year was done, and whether a graduate program requires CPT from the start. These are the school's facts. Duly never computes a school's calendar.
15. Whether the program end date moved, and when the change was asked for.
16. Whether every term was a full course load, and whether online classes stayed within the limit. Duly asks this because it does not check terms yet.

Duly works these out and never asks for them: the level of a card, same or higher level (a reading), the end date in force, the day a move ends OPT, a change of employer, and every count.

The order follows the documents a student holds: the current I-20 first, then older I-20s, newest first, then the EAD cards for each program, then everyday facts, then a check of the whole record. A student with one program and no training answers about ten screens. After onboarding, the engine's questions come one at a time in the same style.

**Step 1 of 5: Your program now**

1. "Add your current I-20." Buttons: "Add my I-20", "Type it in". Why: "Your I-20 holds your school, level, field and dates. Duly reads it on this computer, and you check each field before Duly uses it."
2. School name, and the school code if the I-20 shows it.
3. "Your education level, as your I-20 shows it": Associate, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, English language, Other. Why: "Many rules count by level, such as 12 months of OPT at each level."
4. "Your major, as your I-20 shows it," and the CIP code beside it. Why: "Duly does not match your major to any list for you."
5. "Is this degree on the STEM Designated Degree Program List?" Yes, No, or "I'm not sure". Why: "Your DSO can tell you. Duly does not guess it from your major's name."
6. The program start and end dates on this I-20.
7. "Has your DSO changed this program's end date?" If yes, for each change: the earlier date, the day you asked, the day it was granted, and why.
8. "Are you still in this program?" Still studying, or Finished. If finished: the day all course requirements were done, and the conferral day, or "Not conferred yet".
9. "Is this program part of a dual degree?" If yes, the other program, with the same school filled in.
10. "In every term, did you take a full course load, or have your DSO's approval first for a lighter one?" Then: "In every term, was no more than one class, or 3 credits, of your full load online?" Why: "Duly does not check your terms yet. If the answer is no or not sure, Duly drafts a question for your DSO."

**Step 2 of 5: Earlier study**

1. "Before this program, did you study in another program in the US on an F-1?" Why: "Earlier programs decide how much OPT and CPT you have used, and which degrees a STEM extension can rest on."
2. For each earlier program, newest first: questions 2 to 9 of Step 1, from its I-20. Then: "How did you move from <School, level> to <School, level>?" The choices are: "Transferred to another school", "New level at the same school", "Left the US and came back on a new I-20". Then that move's dates: the day you told the school, the release date, the new I-20's date, and the day you contacted the new DSO.
3. "Is that every program you studied in the US on an F-1?" Buttons: "That's every program", "Add another program".
4. "Do you have a degree from a school outside the US, or from a US school while not on an F-1?" If yes: level, field, where, conferral day, and the STEM list question for a US degree. Why: "The rule for a STEM extension names a degree from a U.S. educational institution. Duly asks so it does not assume either way."

**Step 3 of 5: Permission to work**, for each program, newest first

1. "During <program>, did you have CPT?" For each CPT: its dates on the I-20; full or part time, as the DSO marked it; the employer; the day the DSO signed the I-20 for it. If a CPT started early, ask the first-year question, and at graduate level the CPT-from-the-start question.
2. "During or after <program>, did you have OPT?" For each: before or after the program end date (and full or part time, if before); the recommendation date; the filing date; the EAD dates ("Add my EAD card" or "Type the dates"), or the decision so far.
3. "Did you get a STEM extension after this OPT?" For each: its dates, and "Which degree is it based on?", with "I'm not sure" available.
4. When two OPTs share a level: "Did your DSO note in SEVIS that you are splitting OPT between these programs?"
5. "Is that all the CPT and OPT for <program>?"

**Step 4 of 5: Jobs, trips and H-1B**

1. For each job: the employer; the start; the end, or "Still working here"; hours a week, and any change of hours; "Which permission was this job under?" (Duly proposes the card whose dates hold the start, and the student confirms). Ask E-Verify only for a STEM job or step. Then "Is that every job since <first training start>?"
2. "Have you left the US since <the earliest program start>?" For each trip: the day you left; the day you came back, or "Still away"; what it was (job travel, leave your employer approved, personal, a study abroad term); which I-20 you showed; its travel signature date; and whether you had a job to return to.
3. "Has an employer filed an H-1B petition for you?" For each: the filing day; the receipt day; the start day asked for; whether it asks to change status in the US; whether it is under the yearly cap; what has happened with it, and on what day; the approved start; and the day H-1B began.

**Step 5 of 5: Check and finish**

1. The record as a timeline: each program with its training, moves and trips, in order, each date with its source. Buttons: "This is everything", "Change something".
2. Typed dates (D59): "Did you type these dates from your documents?", then each date checked against its document.
3. Time zone, proposed from the computer and confirmed.
4. "You're set.", with the programs, where the record stands, and what Duly watches (from `upcoming`), and "Everything lives in Your case and can be changed any time." Button: "Open Duly".
